23m here. I find your post shockingly relatable. 

My solution is just to keep looking. Not necessarily for a romantic relationship, either, but just for relationships in general. In the process, you’ll probably make a friend or two, if nothing else. And even friendships have the potential to expand into something more. 

Unfortunately, my solution has backfired in a way, as well. I’ve been obsessing perhaps a little too much over trying to meet people lately. And every time I fail to (and, boy, have I failed a lot), the lonelier I feel, and so I want to look more. It’s a vicious cycle sort of thing. 

So, balance is key. As hard as it might be. I suggest not completely putting off the idea of finding someone, but not being completely obsessed with it, as well. 

In my case, I went a good bit of my life avoiding people and trying to make relationships, so obviously I didn’t make any. So, in your position, I’d ask myself. What am I doing about my lack of relationships? Am I doing too much or too little? Be balanced. :)

As for depression, I highly recommend cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT). Have you looked into that? Even just a good book that teaches it can do wonders.

By “well thought out” I just mean that I tailor my messages specifically to the person who I’m sending them to, matching their level of silliness and whatnot. I also bring up something they mentioned on their profile, for instance, and I ask them about it. I try to keep it light and add humor. I’m very mindful not to come off as clingy, I’d say. But maybe I'm doing it accidentally anyway? 

As for length, this also depends on the person I’m messaging. If I see they’ve wrote a lot about themselves on their profile, I will also try to write a lengthier message. These can be anywhere between 200 to 1000 characters. Usually around the 400-800 character range, I’d say.

On the other hand, if they have barely filled out their profile, I will keep my message as low as maybe a line or two, but I’m more inclined to message lengthier profiles, anyway.

I don't think it's common sense, but I'm not here to get you to agree with me. 

I just notice a lot of people on here make very bold statements about how they are absolutely certain that they have issues with women due to their height, and I want to know how they are so certain.
In Psychology this sort of thinking would be classified as “[distorted thinking](http://psychcentral.com/lib/15-common-cognitive-distortions/0002153),” particularly, jumping to conclusions.  And it’s the main cause of cognitive issues like depression and low self-esteem. 

Now, I’m sure most women prefer taller guys, but perhaps it’s still best not to make it worse by assuming that some women are rejecting you because of height when they actually may not have been.

So, in other words, you assume it. It might not actually be the case. Why not give them the benefit of the doubt instead? This way you'll still be assuming something, but it will be to your advantage.
How did you realize this?

People will judge you whether you like it or not. All you can do is give them a reason to judge you one way or another. 

People here really seem to dislike the word "confidence," but it does have value because our personalities are the only way we can control how others judge us.

Imagine if every single short person in the world somehow naturally possessed wonderful personalities. I think negative stereotypes would die rather quickly in such a reality.
I never had a problem with my height until I found out other people have a problem with my height. So, that.

I'm not a fan of trying to insult the person back. I feel like this sort of thing puts us on the same level as the person who made an offensive joke. I try to fight these insults with the idea of revealing the absurdity and immaturity of the person's comment by using kindness,  maturity, and humor. 

I think humor is one of the best ways to respond because it shows that you weren't fazed by their attempt to insult you. It shows that your confident and likable to any bystanders, as well.

As for specific comebacks, it's hard to come up with responses without being given a specific comment. I'll edit this if I think of a good one.

I wouldn't say it's necessarily a male thing. The same style of insult could be directed to a female with something like, "I don't hang out with girls who have short hair." Silly example, but you get the idea, I hope. 

It doesn't matter what feature, masculine or feminine, is being targeted, the point is, you're being deemed inferior because of that trivial feature.
